b2-31-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Cooked Until Tender
b2-31-01.scenario: At the inn in Óbuda, the innkeeper asks you, the cook's helper, what to do with the beef for Szindbád's soup.
b2-31-01.prompt: Tell the innkeeper how the beef must be cooked.
cues: Say what state it must reach
b2-31-01.english: We braise the beef slowly until tender.
b2-31-01.canDo: I can use resultative sublative phrases (-ra/-re) to describe the final state of culinary transformations

b2-31-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Like Grandmother's Kitchen
b2-31-02.scenario: Szindbád smells the soup that the innkeeper has brought and asks you what it smells like to you.
b2-31-02.prompt: Tell Szindbád what the smell is like.
cues: Say what the smell is like
b2-31-02.target: Olyan az illata, mintha a nagymamám főzte volna.
b2-31-02.english: It smells as if my grandmother had cooked it.
b2-31-02.canDo: I can construct vivid sensory similes using mintha combined with the conditional mood

b2-31-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Meat and Wine
b2-31-03.scenario: The innkeeper pours Szindbád a glass of dry wine and asks you how the meat and the wine taste.
b2-31-03.prompt: Tell the innkeeper how the meat and the wine are.
b2-31-03.target: A hús omlós és zamatos, a bor pedig fanyar.
b2-31-03.english: The meat is tender and flavorful, and the wine is tart.
b2-31-03.canDo: I can describe food with omlós, zamatos and fanyar

b2-31-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Toast at the Table
b2-31-04.scenario: The innkeeper asks you, as the guest of honour, to say a few words before Szindbád's table starts to drink.
b2-31-04.prompt: Give a short toast to the host.
cues: Invite the guests to raise their glasses
Name whose health you drink to
b2-31-04.target: Emeljük poharunkat a házigazda egészségére, és koccintsunk együtt!
b2-31-04.english: Let us raise our glasses to the host's health, and let us clink glasses together!
b2-31-04.canDo: I can formulate polite formal toasts and expressions of hospitality (pohárköszöntő)

b2-31-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Line for the Review
b2-31-05.scenario: A newspaper editor asks you for one sentence about the inn's soup for a restaurant review.
b2-31-05.prompt: Tell the editor one sentence for the review about the soup and the price.
cues: Say what the soup was like
Say how the value for money is
b2-31-05.target: A leves kifogástalan volt, és az ár-érték arány kedvező.
b2-31-05.english: The soup was flawless, and the value for money is favorable.
b2-31-05.canDo: I can write a short sentence reviewing a dish or a restaurant (étteremkritika)

b2-31-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What We Ate
b2-31-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the evening Szindbád asks you to sum up the meal.
b2-31-consolidation.prompt: Tell Szindbád how the meat was cooked and what the meal felt like.
cues: Say how the meat was cooked
Compare the meal to something familiar
b2-31-consolidation.target: A húst puhára párolták, és olyan finom volt, mintha otthon ettünk volna.
b2-31-consolidation.english: They braised the meat until tender, and it was so good as if we had eaten at home.
b2-31-consolidation.canDo: I can use resultative -ra/-re phrases to say how food is cooked (pirosra süt, puhára párol)
